title: He didn’t choose sin.
paragraphs:
He didn’t choose sin.
He chose what looked safe.
And that’s how it started.

Lot didn’t wake up one morning and say, “I want to live near wickedness.”
Genesis 13:10 says he lifted his eyes and saw that the Jordan Valley was “well watered… like the garden of the Lord.” It looked like Eden.
But it was leaning toward Sodom.
And verse 13 quietly drops the truth we often ignore: “Now the men of Sodom were wicked, great sinners against the Lord.”

He saw blessing.
God saw danger.

And here’s the tension you can’t ignore—
sometimes the thing you’re praying for… is positioned right next to what can destroy you.
Let that sit.
Because if we’re honest, we’ve done the same.

We didn’t plan to drift.
We just stood a little closer.
Stayed a little longer.
Compromised a little quieter.
No one posts about that part.

The slow fade.
The silent compromise.
The “it’s not that bad” decisions we baptize with excuses.

Lot didn’t run into Sodom.
He pitched his tents toward it (Genesis 13:12).
That’s the part that should shake you.
Because direction eventually becomes destination.

AHA REVELATION:
You don’t have to choose evil to end up in it—you just have to choose what looks better over what God said.
And some of you are there right now.

Not fully in sin.
But facing it.

Entertaining it.
Justifying proximity to it.

You still pray.
Still worship.
Still show up.
But your heart?
Divided.

SPIRITUAL MIRROR:
You’re not far from God… but you’re facing the wrong direction.
Read that again.

We love to talk about big, obvious sins.
But what about delayed obedience?
What about the job that pays more but slowly starves your soul?
What about the relationship that feels right but pulls you away from Christ?
What about the secret habit you keep hidden because “it’s manageable”?

Be honest—
what are you standing too close to?
And here’s the dangerous part:

You can look blessed…
and still be one decision away from breaking.

Lot gained land.
But later lost peace, influence, and almost his family (Genesis 19).
Because what you gain outside God’s will… will cost more than you think.
But here’s where grace breaks in.

Abram didn’t fight for the land.
He trusted God.
And after Lot chose what looked better, God told Abram, “Lift up your eyes… all the land that you see I will give to you” (Genesis 13:14–15).
Did you catch that?

Lot lifted his eyes without God.
Abram lifted his eyes with God.

Same action.
Different outcome.

One chose by sight.
The other received by promise.
And this is where Jesus steps into your story.
Because every one of us has been Lot.

We’ve chosen what felt right instead of what was right.
We’ve leaned toward sin, flirted with compromise, and called it wisdom.
Romans 3:23 says “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”

That includes you.
That includes me.
But here’s the Gospel:
Jesus didn’t stay distant from our compromise.
He stepped into it.

He took the judgment we deserved—just like Sodom faced—upon Himself at the cross.
He bore our sin, our drift, our hidden compromises.

So that through Him, we don’t just escape destruction—
we receive a new direction.

Grace doesn’t just forgive you.
It reorients you.

Conviction line:
Some of you want God’s promises while still facing Sodom. That’s not faith—that’s self-deception.
But hear this with hope—

You are not too far gone.
You are not too compromised.
You are not too late.
In Christ, you are called out, cleaned, and given a new inheritance.

Identity shift:
You are not a person who manages sin.
You are a person who is called to walk in holiness through Jesus.
This is your moment.
Turn.

Not slowly.
Not halfway.
Fully.
Because repentance is not shame—it’s alignment.
And Jesus is ready to meet you there.
